name: git add
title: Stage changes for the next commit
description: Adds file contents to the staging area (index) so they are included in the next commit. Staging is a snapshot of the file at the time you ran the command - later edits need to be staged again.

flags.name: --all
flags.description: Stage every change in the working tree, including deletions.

flags.name: --patch
flags.description: Interactively choose which hunks within a file to stage.

flags.name: --update
flags.description: Stage modifications and deletions, but not untracked files.

examples.explanation: Stages all changes in the current directory and below.
Stages one specific file.

risk.sideEffects: Updates the staging area only; working tree files are untouched.

name: git restore
title: Discard working tree changes or unstage files
description: Restores files in the working tree or the staging area. Without --staged it overwrites your local edits, which cannot be recovered - review 'git diff' before running it.

flags.name: --staged
flags.description: Remove the file from the staging area while keeping working tree edits.

flags.name: --source
flags.description: Restore content from a specific commit rather than the index.

examples.explanation: Unstages the file but keeps your edits on disk.
Permanently discards uncommitted edits to that file.

risk.sideEffects: Without --staged, uncommitted edits are overwritten and lost.
risk.reversibility: Irreversible unless the change was previously committed or stashed.

name: git checkout
title: Switch branches or restore files
description: Switches the working tree to another branch or commit. This is the older, multi-purpose command; 'git switch' and 'git restore' split its two jobs and are clearer for new work.

flags.name: -b
flags.description: Create the branch and switch to it in one step.

flags.name: --track
flags.description: Set up the new branch to track a remote branch.

examples.explanation: Switches the working tree to the main branch.
Creates a new branch and switches to it.

risk.sideEffects: Rewrites working tree files to match the target branch. Refuses to run if it would overwrite uncommitted changes.
risk.reversibility: Reversible by checking out the previous branch.

name: git switch
title: Switch to another branch
description: Switches branches. Introduced in Git 2.23 as a clearer replacement for the branch-switching half of 'git checkout'. It will not silently discard uncommitted work.

flags.name: --create
flags.description: Create a new branch and switch to it.

flags.name: --detach
flags.description: Switch to a commit without attaching to a branch.

examples.explanation: Switches to the main branch.
Creates the branch feature/login and switches to it.

risk.sideEffects: Updates working tree files to match the target branch.

name: git clone
title: Clone a repository into a new directory
description: Copies a remote repository, including its full history, into a new local directory and sets up 'origin' as the default remote.

flags.name: --depth
flags.description: Create a shallow clone with a limited history, which is much faster.

flags.name: --branch
flags.description: Check out a specific branch instead of the default.

examples.explanation: Clones the repository into a ./project directory.
Clones only the latest commit for a faster download.

risk.sideEffects: Creates a new directory and downloads repository data over the network.
risk.reversibility: Reversible by deleting the created directory.

name: git pull
title: Fetch and integrate changes from a remote
description: Downloads commits from the remote branch and merges them into the current branch. It is 'git fetch' followed by 'git merge', so it can produce merge conflicts.

flags.name: --rebase
flags.description: Replay local commits on top of the remote branch instead of merging.

flags.name: --ff-only
flags.description: Abort rather than create a merge commit if the update is not a fast-forward.

examples.explanation: Fetches and merges the tracked remote branch.
Rebases local commits on top of origin/main for a linear history.

risk.sideEffects: Modifies the working tree and may create a merge commit or leave conflicts to resolve.

name: git push
title: Upload local commits to a remote repository
description: Sends commits from a local branch to the remote. A plain push is safe; --force can overwrite commits other people depend on.

flags.name: --set-upstream
flags.description: Push and record the remote branch as the tracking branch.

flags.name: --force-with-lease
flags.description: Force push, but abort if the remote has commits you have not seen. Safer than --force.

flags.name: --tags
flags.description: Push tags along with commits.

examples.explanation: Pushes the current branch to its tracked remote branch.
Pushes a new branch and sets it to track origin.

risk.sideEffects: Publishes commits to a shared remote where others can see them.
risk.reversibility: Published history is hard to retract; a force push can destroy others' commits.

name: git init
title: Create an empty Git repository
description: Initialises a new Git repository in the current directory by creating a .git subdirectory. Existing files are left untouched and remain untracked until staged.

flags.name: --bare
flags.description: Create a repository with no working tree, used for shared server-side remotes.

flags.name: --initial-branch
flags.description: Set the name of the initial branch.

examples.explanation: Initialises a repository in the current directory.
Creates my-project with main as the initial branch.

name: git revert
title: Undo a commit by creating a new one
description: Creates a new commit that reverses the changes of an earlier commit. Unlike 'git reset', it does not rewrite history, which makes it the safe way to undo work that has already been pushed.

flags.name: --no-commit
flags.description: Stage the reversal without creating the commit automatically.

flags.name: --mainline
flags.description: Specify which parent to treat as the mainline when reverting a merge.

examples.explanation: Creates a commit that undoes the most recent commit.
Stages the reversal so you can review before committing.

risk.sideEffects: Adds a new commit and modifies working tree files.
risk.reversibility: Reversible - the original commit remains in history.

name: git remote
title: View and manage remote repositories
description: Lists, adds, and removes the named remote repositories your local repository can fetch from and push to.

flags.name: -v
flags.description: Show the fetch and push URLs for each remote.

examples.explanation: Lists every remote with its fetch and push URLs.
Adds a remote named origin.
